conclusion: Per-image complete vision-feature caching has structural support; numerical equivalence and realistic timing remain unproved. Prioritize the separate grid-only vision attention candidate first.

mechanism.evidence: Preprocessing iterates images separately and derives token count from grid.
Visual positions are per-image grid based; attention segment lengths are h*w repeated t times.
Visual forward returns primary embedding plus all three DeepStack feature arrays.
Noncausal visual self attention receives per-segment starts and lengths.
Kernel accesses independent Q/KV segment starts and lengths.
Supplying inputs_embeds directly bypasses visual forward and leaves DeepStack unset; reject this shortcut.
Native language mRoPE derives from full current multimodal start/end positions and must remain unchanged.

candidate_design.boundary: Memoize complete visual() return per image, including primary+three DeepStack arrays; slice by grid.prod()/merge_size**2, restore original order and duplicates
candidate_design.scope: Static images t=1, per-episode bounded cache, cold start, no prepopulation from measured future inputs
candidate_design.memory: For observed 300 tokens/image: 300*2560*2*4=6144000 bytes/image; 96 entries 562.5MiB, 200 entries1171.875MiB before allocator and assembly overhead

required_validation: Original nine-image batch vs per-image/miss-only batch primary and all DeepStack errors; batch shapes may change Conv3d/F.linear algorithm and rounding.
Partial hits, reordering, duplicate images, mixed grids, eviction and unchanged full input/mRoPE contracts.
Tokens, natural EOS and navigation actions/quality; mathematical independence does not guarantee bitwise equivalence.
Replay a frozen real chronological history with image reconstruction checks; cold cache each episode; compare FP16 off/on and AWQ off/on under identical load.
Report first request, subsequent requests, hit/miss/eviction, total episode time, peak memory and host lookup/hash/assembly cost.
Repetition of one fixed request with fully warm cache is not general navigation or quantization evidence.
attribution: Any common visual-compute savings are system improvements. Equal savings can enlarge endpoint-relative quantization advantage without making quantized language kernels themselves faster.
